This appeal coming on for hearing this day, Hon'ble Shri Justice Milind Ramesh Phadke passed the following:
 JUDGMENT 1.

This first appeal under Section 28 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (for short "the Act") is preferred against the judgment and decree dated 18.05.2012 passed in H.M.A. Case No.28 of 2011 by the First Additional District Judge Datia, whereby the application preferred by the respondent under section 13 of the Act on the ground of cruelty was decreed and the marriage between the appellant and respondent was held to be dissolved.

sentences.text: Short facts of the case are that marriage between appellant and respondent was solemnized on 19.02.2003 as per Hindu rites and rituals and they started living thereafter as husband and wife.
It has been alleged that certain articles and ornaments were given at the time of marriage and there was dissentment and dissatisfaction in that regard.
Immediately after the marriage, the in-laws started demanding dowry and started harassing the respondent wife and she was thrown out of the house.

Thereafter on 06.06.2006 she had to lodge a complaint under section 498-A of IPC against appellant/husband and another case under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. for maintenance was filed and a case under the Domestic Violence Act was also preferred.

The appellant and his family members have abandoned the respondent for more than five years without any proper and sufficient reason and the appellant has not even established physical relations with the respondent.
Therefore the respondent filed a case for dissolution of marriage.
3. The written statement has been filed by the appellant before the learned trial Court in which it has been mentioned that a false case has been lodged against him.

The allegations pertaining to harassment are absolutely false because the respondent was residing in the maternal house at Datia and the respondent herself was not residing with the appellant and the date on which she has levelled the allegation of cruelty against the appellant, the appellant was suffering from Tuberculosis.

A false case under Section 498-A of IPC has been lodged by the respondent by creating a false ground pertaining to cruelty and an application under section 125 Cr.P.C was also submitted,
but the application for interim maintenance has been rejected by the court below.

The respondent was living separately without any good and sufficient reason and mental cruelty was in fact committed by the respondent and a frivolous case has been filed against the appellant, and therefore, appellant wants to get dissolved the marriage with the respondent.
4. Learned Trial Court after due appreciation of evidence found the cruelty committed by the appellant to be proved and accordingly granted a decree of divorce under section 13 of the Act.
Aggrieved by the aforesaid, the present appeal has been preferred by the husband.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant had tried to assail the said order contending that the impugned judgment and decree passed by learned trial court is manifestly illegal, arbitrary without jurisdiction and contrary to law, therefore, deserves to be set aside.
It is also submitted that the complete case revolves around the allegation pertaining to cruelty.
The documentary proof which has been submitted by the respondent/wife for the purpose of proving the cruelty, are all concocted piece of documentary proof.
The letter has never been sent from Delhi to Datia, those are concocted one as there is no seal of Delhi.
This aspect of the matter that the wife is willing to use the evidence by forging it has not been considered by learned trial Court.
Thus, the illegality has been committed in relying over the document and giving finding pertaining to cruelty.
The second aspect is with regard to holding that the desertion of wife is proper.
Both these findings as has been arrived at by learned Court are running in self-conflict.

6. It was further submitted that the learned Court has stated that when the wife was residing at Datia, she has been subjected to cruelty while the wife has stated that at that time she was pursuing her studies.
In such circumstances when there are major contradictions, the impugned judgment passed by learned trial Court is not sustainable.

sentences.text: It was further contended that grave illegality has been committed by learned Trial Court while giving the finding pertaining to cruelty.
The version of the respondent in this context was required to be seen.

On the one hand, she is making a statement pertaining to cruelty and on the other she is making a statement that at that time she was pursuing her studies, hence it is a total misuse of process of Court for the purpose of gaining the financial benefit by virtue of filing of application under Section 125 of Cr.P.C.
8.

It was further submitted that the learned trial Court so far as the allegation pertaining to desertion was concerned, has not considered that it was the respondent who had deserted the appellant, as she has admitted that she was pursuing her studies as a regular student at Datia.

This explanation saves the appellant and strengthens his argument and allegation that the fact of cruelty committed by him at Delhi is falsified by the fact that at that period the wife had been pursuing her studies as a regular student at Datia.

Further, it is argued that the case lodged at Datia is a concocted proof pertaining to cruelty upon her, which has been created in fact for the purpose of forging the evidence and the Court in this regard should have registered the case against the wife of perjury as there was due proof in that regard.

Further, it is submitted that there is absolutely no document on record to show that who caused the cruelty upon the respondent, what kind of cruelty has been caused and when it has been caused, yet learned Trial Court has held that the cruelty has been caused towards the wife in absence of specific proof in that regard, thus, such findings are not sustainable particularly when it is in the nature of castigation.
9.

It is also submitted that there was an admission on the part of respondent that when the appellant/husband was seriously ill, she was not residing with him, which goes to show that she had not taken care of appellant even when he was seriously ill.
Thus, towards whom the cruelty has been committed should have been presumed by learned Trial Court.
Thus, the illegality is apparent and clear on record.

10. It is further submitted that the wife herself on the one hand stated that she was residing at Delhi and on the other hand she has admitted in her cross-examination that she had been pursuing her studies of PGDCA and B.Ed and was doing regular duties as teacher at Datia.

In such circumstances,
reliance which has been placed by learned Trial Court for the purpose of giving a finding pertaining to cruelty being committed by the appellant is not at all sustainable in the eye of law.

11. It is also submitted that the wife upto 3 years of marriage has never complained of impotency of her husband or had refused to consummate the marriage and now has levelled a false allegation of impotency against the appellant, which amounts to cruelty.

Further, it is also submitted that most of the family members were not residing with the appellant in the matrimonial house, against whom the cruelty had been alleged, thus, the very complaint of harassment of respondent on account of demand of dowry was an afterthought, thus, it was prayed that the appeal be allowed and the impugned judgment and decree passed by learned Trial Court be set aside.
12. None appears for the respondent.

13. Heard learned counsel for the appellant and perused the record.

sentences.text: A decree of divorce has been granted in favour of the respondent/wife on the basis of physical and mental cruelty committed by the appellant/husband, desertion and denial of the marital happiness.

15. Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act provides for grant of divorce in certain cases where any marriage solemnized, whether before or after the commencement of this Act, may be dissolved by a decree of divorce on the grounds specified therein.
Decree under Clause (ia) of Sub-Section (I) of Section 13 of the Act may be passed by the Court on the ground that after the solemnization of the marriage, the wife was treated with cruelty.

16. It is well settled law that the expression 'cruelty' includes both (i) physical cruelty; and (ii)
mental cruelty.

The concept of mental cruelty has been dealt with in Halsbury's Laws of England as under:-
"The general rule in all cases of cruelty is that the entire matrimonial relationship must be considered, and that rule is of special value when the cruelty consists not of violent acts but of injurious reproaches, complaints, accusations or taunts.

In cases where no violence is averred, it is undesirable to consider judicial pronouncements with a view to creating certain categories of acts or conduct as having or lacking the nature or quality which renders them capable or incapable in all circumstances of amounting to cruelty; for it is the effect of the conduct rather than its nature which is of paramount importance in assessing a complaint of cruelty.
Whether one spouse has been guilty of cruelty to the other is essentially a question of fact and previously decided cases have little, if any, value.

17. In Gollins V. Gollins 1964 AC 644: reported in (1963) 2 All ER 966, Lord Reid stated as follows:-
"No one has ever attempted to give a comprehensive definition of cruelty and I do not intend to try to do so.

entities.text: Gollins V. Gollins 1964 AC 644: reported in (1963) 2 All ER 966
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Much must depend on the knowledge and intention of the respondent, on the nature of his (or her) conduct, and on the character and physical or mental weakness of the spouses, and probably no general statement is equally applicable in all cases except the requirement that the party seeking relief must show actual or probable injury to life, limb or health".

18. The test of cruelty has been laid down by Hon'ble Apex court in the leading case of N.G. Dastane vs. S. Dastane reported in (1975) 2 SCC 326, thus:

sentences.text: "30. ......The inquiry, therefore, has to be whether the conduct charged as cruelty is of such a character as to cause in the mind of the petitioner a reasonable apprehension that it will be harmful or injurious for him to live with the respondent. ....."
19. In Shobha Rani vs. Madhukar Reddi reported in (1988) 1 SCC 105, the Hon'ble Supreme Court examined the concept of cruelty.

entities.text: Shobha Rani vs. Madhukar Reddi reported in (1988) 1 SCC 105
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was observed that the term 'cruelty' has not been defined in the Hindu Marriage Act.
It has been used in Section 13(1) (ia) of the Act in the context of human conduct and behavior in relation to or in respect of matrimonial duties or obligations.
It is a course of conduct of one spouse which adversely affects the other spouse.
The cruelty may be mental or physical, intentional or unintentional.
If it is physical, it is a question of degree which is relevant.
If it is mental, the enquiry must begin as to the nature of the cruel treatment and then as to the impact of such treatment on the mind of the other spouse.

Whether it caused reasonable apprehension that it would be harmful or injurious to live with the other, ultimately, is a matter of inference to be drawn by taking into account the nature of the conduct and its effect on the complaining spouse.
There may, however, be cases where the conduct complained of itself is bad enough and per se unlawful or illegal.
Then the impact or the injurious effect on the other spouse need not be enquired into or considered.
In such cases, the cruelty will be established if the conduct itself is proved or admitted.
The absence of intention should not make any difference in the case, if by ordinary sense in human affairs, the act complained of could otherwise be regarded as cruelty.
Mens rea is not a necessary element in cruelty.
The relief to the party cannot be denied on the ground that there has been no deliberate or willful ill-treatment.

20. In the matter of Samar Ghosh vs. Jaya Ghosh reported in (2007) 4 SCC 511, the Hon'ble Apex court in para 101 has held as under:
"101.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: No uniform standard can ever be laid down for guidance, yet we deem it appropriate to enumerate some instances of human behavior which may be relevant in dealing with the cases of 'mental cruelty'.
The instances indicated in the succeeding paragraphs are only illustrative and not exhaustive.

(i) On consideration of complete matrimonial life of the parties, acute mental pain,
agony and suffering as would not make possible for the parties to live with each other could come within the broad parameters of mental cruelty.

(ii) On comprehensive appraisal of the entire matrimonial life of the parties, it becomes abundantly clear that situation is such that the wronged party cannot reasonably be asked to put up with such conduct and continue to live with other party.

(iii) Mere coldness or lack of affection cannot amount to cruelty, frequent rudeness of language, petulance of manner, indifference and neglect may reach such a degree that it makes the married life for the other spouse absolutely intolerable.

sentences.text: (iv) Mental cruelty is a state of mind.

The feeling of deep anguish, disappointment,
frustration in one spouse caused by the conduct of other for a long time may lead to mental cruelty.

(v) A sustained course of abusive and humiliating treatment calculated to torture,
discommode or render miserable life of the spouse.
(vi) Sustained unjustifiable conduct and 11ehavior of one spouse actually affecting physical and mental health of the other spouse.
The treatment complained of and the resultant danger or apprehension must be very grave, substantial and weighty.

(vii) Sustained reprehensible conduct, studied neglect, indifference or total departure from the normal standard of conjugal kindness causing injury to mental health or deriving sadistic pleasure can also amount to mental cruelty.

(viii) The conduct must be much more than jealousy, selfishness, possessiveness,
which causes unhappiness and dissatisfaction and emotional upset may not be a ground for grant of divorce on the ground of mental cruelty.
(ix) Mere trivial irritations, quarrels, normal wear and tear of the married life which happens in day to day life would not be adequate for grant of divorce on the ground of mental cruelty.
(x) The married life should be reviewed as a whole and a few isolated instances over a period of years will not amount to cruelty.

The ill-conduct must be persistent for a fairly lengthy period, where the relationship has deteriorated to an extent that because of the acts and 11ehavior of a spouse, the wronged party finds it extremely difficult to live with the other party any longer, may amount to mental cruelty.

(xi) If a husband submits himself for an operation of sterilization without medical reasons and without the consent or knowledge of his wife and similarly if the wife undergoes vasectomy or abortion without medical reason or without the consent or knowledge of her husband, such an act of the spouse may lead to mental cruelty.
(xii) Unilateral decision of refusal to have intercourse for considerable period without there being any physical incapacity or valid reason may amount to mental cruelty.
(xiii) Unilateral decision of either husband or wife after marriage not to have child from the marriage may amount to cruelty.
(xiv) Where there has been a long period of continuous separation, it may fairly be concluded that the matrimonial bond is beyond repair.
The marriage becomes a fiction though supported by a legal tie.

By refusing to sever that tie, the law in such cases, does not serve the sanctity of marriage; on the contrary, it shows scant regard Amit Pachauri vs Smt. Himani Tiwari on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19084924/
6 for the feelings and emotions of the parties.

sentences.text: In such like situations, it may lead to mental cruelty."

21. Now coming to the facts of the case from the evidence of the appellant, AW1 and AW2 Dr. R.K.
Tiwari and the documents submitted in support of the contentions, the learned trial Court has held that there is no reason to disbelieve the letters dated 09.06.2004, 22.06.2004 and 24.01.2006,
wherein the cruelty allegedly committed by the appellant/husband and his family members upon the respondent/wife was narrated and there was no specific denial or contention that the said letters were concocted documents, neither they have been controverted or challenged in the cross-examination of the respondent/wife nor any evidence has been adduced to prove the factum of they being concocted and since those letters were sent through post, the very allegation of harassment, physical and mental both, could not be denied and the finding in that regard cannot in absence of any rebuttal be said to be a perverse finding.
22.

Another fact which is required to be taken note of is that the appellant/husband himself in para 17 of his written statement had sought a decree for divorce and had stated in specific words that he does not want to live with the respondent/wife and the only challenge as per para 22 of the written statement was to the grounds on which the decree was sought by the respondent/wife which itself made it clear to the learned Trial Court that it was husband himself who was responsible for deserting the wife.
23.

Further an allegation of mental ill-health of the respondent/wife had been taken by the appellant in his written statement, wherein allegation of the respondent/wife being suffering from epilepsy has been made, but neither any medical evidence had been produced in support of the above contention nor any doctor has been examined to prove the said factum which has been held to be a ground of mental cruelty committed by the appellant/husband upon the wife which in the light of the judgments cited above can be said to be a genuine ground for holding it to be a mental cruelty and a good ground for divorce.

24. So far as denial of the marital happiness to the respondent/wife by the appellant/husband is concerned, in para 39 of the judgment the learned trial Court while taking note of paragraph 45 of the cross- examination of the respondent/wife had observed that the aforesaid allegation has not been controverted.

It has further been observed by the learned trial Court that though in that regard no direct evidence could be available, but from the conduct of the appellant, it would be clear that since he himself had deserted the respondent/wife and had not made any efforts for taking her back home is enough to conclude that he had denied the respondent/wife with the marital happiness and,
therefore, is held to be a ground for divorce, which according to this Court after going through the statement of the respondent/wife and the statement of the appellant appears to be wholly justified.
25.

Further from the FIR registered against the appellant under Section 498A of the IPC and the Dowry Prohibition Act, it would be evident that the respondent/wife was being harassed on account of demand of dowry regarding which matter is pending before the competent Court at Datia in which challan has already been filed and whether the said FIR or charge-sheet has been quashed by a competent Court or the matter has resulted in acquittal has not been placed by the appellant Amit Pachauri vs Smt. Himani Tiwari on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19084924/
7 before this Court which also goes to show that the respondent/wife was subjected to cruelty at the hands of the appellant and his family members and in that regard the finding of the learned trial Court of committing cruelty cannot be said to be unsustainable.

entities.text: Amit Pachauri vs Smt. Himani Tiwari
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 26. Thus, the decree of divorce has been granted in favour of the wife on the basis of mental and physical cruelty committed by the appellant/husband, which has been proved before the learned Trial Court by leading ample evidence which could not be controverted or rebutted in an effective manner by the appellant.
Therefore, this Court concludes that the learned trial Court has rightly passed the judgment and decree for divorce, dissolving the marriage between the parties.
27. Accordingly, the present appeal being sans merit is hereby dismissed.

(RAVI MALIMATH) (MILIND RAMESH PHADKE)
 CHIEF JUSTICE JUDGE  ch CHANDNI NARWARIYA 2024.04.25 14:04:03 +05'30'
